questions.question: How does data fetching work in the App Router — Server Components, waterfalls, streaming, and mutations?
questions.title: App Router Data
questions.direct_answer: In Server Components, fetch is the data layer: await fetch() directly in an async component (no useEffect, no loading state in the component). Next extends fetch with memoization (same request de-duped per render) and caching (default cached, opt out with cache: 'no-store' or a revalidate time). Waterfalls — sequential awaits when they could be parallel — are the #1 performance bug: two awaits back-to-back run serially; fix with Promise.all([...]) so independent requests fly together. Streaming: an async component under a Suspense boundary (or a loading.tsx) streams independently — the shell renders instantly and the slow part fills in. Mutations: Server Actions (async functions with 'use server') run on the server, revalidatePath/revalidateTag invalidate the cache, and the router refreshes the affected segments automatically.

sections.title: Interview Answer
Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SC['async Server Component: await fetch at render'] --> MEMO['memoize: same call de-duped per render']
    MEMO --> CACHE['data cache: cached across requests / no-store / revalidate']
    SEQ['sequential awaits'] -->|independent| WF[waterfall — latency adds up]
    WF --> PA['Promise.all: parallel — latency = slowest']
    ASYNC['slow async component under Suspense'] --> STREAM['shell renders instantly, slow part streams']
    SA['Server Action: use server'] --> MUT[mutate + revalidatePath/Tag]
    MUT --> REFRESH[router refetches segments — fresh UI, no client cache]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The cache taxonomy (the layer everyone gets wrong): THREE caches with different scopes — (1) Request Memoization: per-render dedupe (same URL+options within one page render = one fetch) — protects you from a header and a body both calling getUser(); (2) Data Cache: across requests (the fetch is cached and REUSED for other users/renders until revalidation — the default that surprises people: remove it with cache: 'no-store' or time with next: { revalidate: 60 }); (3) Full Route Cache: whole static pages/segments prerendered at build. The 2024 default shift (v15): fetch is no longer cached by default (the community forced it) — GET route handlers and pages still are, but explicit is the new contract; always state your cache intent.

Server vs client fetching (the decision layer): server fetch = secrets, DB, zero client JS, one round trip, SEO; client fetching (useEffect/SWR/React Query) = interactive data that updates without navigation (typeahead, live dashboards), the user's own fast-changing state, and anything after a client event. The pattern that composes them: server fetches the first paint, the client hydrates and takes over live updates — SWR's fallbackData from props is exactly this handoff.

Waterfall depth beyond the same component (the cross-component waterfall): a parent awaiting data to pass as props chains requests even when the child could have fetched its own — the fix is to PUSH the async DOWN into the component that uses the data (each becomes its own Suspense boundary, all requests start in parallel and stream independently — colocation of data and its consumer). The measurement story: look for 'await' as a dependency chain in the flame graph; Next's dev overlay shows segment-by-segment timings. The one-liner: 'data fetching moved INTO render; make independent awaits parallel; stream the slow ones; revalidate after writes' — that's the whole App Router data model.
